title: The text discusses a severe famine crisis in East Africa, referred to as the 'silent famine' due to the lack of attention it is receiving from both foreign and local governments. Aid agencies warn that the situation could lead to a death toll of around 20 million, comparable to the devastating famine of 1984-85. The absence of distressing images in the media is noted as a factor in the lack of urgency for aid. The situation is exacerbated by poor crop yields, rising grain prices, and ongoing conflict in Sudan, which complicates relief efforts. Aid agencies are preparing to launch appeals for assistance, emphasizing the critical months ahead as the famine worsens.
